extracted.intended_audience: leaders and staff of nonprofit newsrooms, prospective INN applicants, and stakeholders in nonprofit journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the Institute for Nonprofit News (INN) membership categories (full, provisional, affiliate), the standards applicants must meet (ethics, transparency, independence, quality/editorial excellence), and the vetting/approval process. Useful for organizations considering or preparing an application to join INN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations applying to join INN are vetted by INN staff to ensure they meet standards for ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as one of the core membership standards (paired with transparency, independence and quality of journalism); INN staff vet applicants against these standards before Board approval. No specific ethical rules are enumerated on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations applying to join INN are vetted by INN staff to ensure they meet standards for transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited repeatedly as a core membership requirement (also referenced as part of 'editorial excellence, independence and transparency' for provisional members). The page does not list concrete transparency measures but frames it as part of the vetting criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations applying to join INN are vetted to ensure they meet standards for independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence is emphasized as a core requirement; for full members this is operationalized as having 501(c)(3) status or editorial independence from their fiscal sponsor. Provisional members often are fiscally sponsored while they work toward full independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of journalism / editorial excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must meet standards for quality of journalism (also described as 'editorial excellence').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page ties quality/editorial excellence to the expectation that full members 'regularly publish original investigative or public service journalism.' Provisional members are described as working to fully meet INN’s membership standards for editorial excellence. Examples of member outlets and beats are provided as context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full member content requirement: original investigative or public service journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Full members of INN regularly publish original investigative or public service journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a defining characteristic of full membership. The page lists multiple newly admitted full members and describes their beats (local/regional investigative, public service reporting) as exemplars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal/organizational requirement: 501(c)(3) status or editorial independence from fiscal sponsor
rubrics_metrics.description: Full members have 501(c)(3) status or editorial independence from their fiscal sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an organization lacks its own nonprofit status, editorial independence from a fiscal sponsor is required. Provisional members are often fiscally sponsored while working toward nonprofit status; the page explains provisional sponsorship as a pathway to meet this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vetting and approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: INN reviews membership applications; applicants are vetted by INN staff and then approved for membership by leading journalists on the INN Board of Directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states INN accepts new members throughout the year and describes a two-step process: staff vetting against membership standards, followed by Board approval. No scoring rubric is provided, but the procedural flow is clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional membership: pathway while meeting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional members receive support while working to fully meet INN’s membership standards for editorial excellence, independence and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional members are often fiscally sponsored to obtain nonprofit status, can access INN’s Network Philanthropy Center for fundraising resources, audience growth support, and benefit from the INN peer community. Provisional status is presented as a transitional category rather than full membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliate membership: mission alignment without newsroom requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Affiliate membership is open to organizations that share the INN mission of advancing nonprofit public service journalism but aren't primarily newsrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiliate members (e.g., News Ambassadors, academic institutions, field-building organizations) can participate in the network even if they do not meet newsroom-specific requirements. The page gives examples (Columbia Journalism School, American Journalism Project) and describes affiliates as organizations that support INN's mission and work in complementary ways.
